heroHeadline: Gallrein Defeats Massie in $32M Kentucky Primary — Trump's Biggest MAGA Scalp; Banking Immigration EO Signed; Taiwan $14B Arms Sale Call Planned
heroSubtitle: Trump-backed challenger Ed Gallrein (former Navy SEAL) defeated seven-term incumbent Rep. Thomas Massie on May 19-20, 2026 in the most expensive House primary in US history ($32.6M total ad spending), with Gallrein winning by ~9 points — Trump's most significant primary scalp of the second term and a direct rebuke of Massie's opposition to the Iran war, the 'One Big Beautiful Bill,' and Epstein file release. On May 20, Trump signed the 'Restoring Integrity to America's Financial System' executive order directing banks to treat customers' immigration status as a financial risk factor and flagging ITIN use, as part of the administration's financial exclusion enforcement architecture against undocumented immigrants. On May 21, Trump announced he is preparing to call Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te ahead of a decision on a $14 billion arms sale to Taiwan — a diplomatically sensitive direct leader-to-leader communication given the US 'one China' policy — and remarked 'I'm right now at 99% in Israel — I could run for prime minister.' Two Capitol Police officers filed suit to block Trump's $1.8 billion political persecution compensation fund, which critics say is designed to benefit January 6 participants. Separately, new polling (Silver Bulletin, May 20) shows Trump's net approval hitting a second-term low of -20.1, with White non-college voters — his core base — collapsing from 63% approval (Feb 2025) to 49% (May 2026). The US-Iran war remains at Day 82 with the naval blockade continuing and the 5-vs-10-year enrichment moratorium gap still unresolved.
